audit_scope: Current Strong Artin, Hodge, Catalan constant and Inverse Galois readers: finite executable layers and explicit geometric/arithmetic/formal boundaries.

audit.scope: Coverage-only construction-to-runtime audit of the four current reader PDFs
audit.source_acquisition: Authorized local complete PDF/text copies; current definitions and scoped mechanism sections inspected, historical crosswalks not treated as authority
audit.claim_boundary: Finite Python/runtime contracts and bounded independent arithmetic replay; not a full proof audit or fresh source research/Lean replay
not_claimed: general rational Hodge proof or counterexample
distinctions: Combinatorial Catalan numbers and the Apéry zeta(3) recurrence are not Catalan-constant rational approximants.
A finite faithful representation is not an actual number-field realization.
Hodge type/packet balance is not an actual rational Chow correspondence.
Finite local lifting or gate reports do not supply arithmetic realization or infinite endpoints.

sources.title: Strong Artin — Cyclic attachment and finite realization
Hodge Conjecture — Cycles, packets and explicit constructors
Catalan’s constant — The arithmetic still required
Inverse Galois — The realization still required

mechanisms.summary: Declared prime-cyclic Clifford order/degree words, induction versus extension, depth and unmet attachment gates.
boundaries: Only internally consistent supplied finite tower data are checked; representation restriction data and automorphic attachment are assumptions.
Prime quotient orders and induction/extension dimension laws are validated; this does not construct a Galois representation.

mechanisms.summary: Explicit finite groups, subgroups, multiplicative linear characters and induced monomial representations.
boundaries: Finite group laws are explicit; character and induced matrices are complex NumPy values with declared tolerances, not general exact cyclotomic coefficients.
There is no automatic irreducible-character-table or invariant-type extension constructor, and no global automorphic induction implementation.

mechanisms.summary: Active characteristic-polynomial coefficient degrees determine which prime-cyclic twists can be separated; trace and determinant are special cases.
boundaries: The runtime has no dedicated exact cyclotomic coefficient-rotation or active-degree selector API.
A coefficient degree divisible by the quotient prime is twist-blind; a finite trace comparison alone does not establish global attachment.

mechanisms.summary: Central characters, sufficiently ramified epsilon data and total induced torsors can fail to distinguish cyclic descents.
boundaries: These are source mathematical no-go statements, not permission to treat a failed selector as successful attachment.
No automated local epsilon-factor or central-character blindness theorem checker is integrated.

mechanisms.summary: Stable H-type multiplicity polynomials in Z[z]/(z^p−1), moving blocks, simultaneous cyclic shifts and common rotational stabilizers.
boundaries: A dedicated H-type decomposition, exact multiplicity-polynomial rotation and alignment-coset implementation is absent.
All stable-type spectra must share the same shift; Fourier zero modes must match, rather than being skipped. Generic cyclic quantum projectors do not supply this type data.

mechanisms.summary: Global attachment is the intersection of the compatible local alignment sets, including all required places.
boundaries: Intersecting a finite user-selected set of local candidates does not establish the intersection over all places.
Split places have the full quotient-character torsor; actual local/global automorphic parameters are external input.

mechanisms.summary: Local Artin descent, temperedness, infinity types, finite Satake roots and cyclotomic Hecke coefficient fields.
boundaries: Classical local Langlands, cyclic base change and cuspidal descent are imported source contracts, not constructed by Python.
There is no general automorphic representation, Satake number-field or infinity-type realization API.

mechanisms.summary: A finite supplied characteristic-zero trace family can be separated by finitely many trace coordinates.
boundaries: The runtime separator uses supplied finite rational trace coordinates, not arbitrary algebraic polynomial alphabets or number-field prime ideals.
Chebotarev existence of actual Frobenius places, good-prime exclusion and Galois/automorphic equality are external mathematical obligations.

mechanisms.summary: Residual trace alphabets, semisimple finite-image bounds, quotient-prime collapse, one-prime residual attachment and finite Satake rigidity.
boundaries: No automatic residual Galois realization, mod-prime pseudocharacter or algebraic coefficient prime-selection constructor is integrated.
Characteristic zero or residual characteristic greater than the dimension is essential to the source trace-faithfulness argument; finite alphabet data alone do not produce an Artin representation.

mechanisms.summary: Explicitly record residual, cohomological, pseudofamily and complex pseudocharacter realization assumptions.
boundaries: Gate reports check supplied Boolean assumptions and return conditional conclusions; they do not construct cohomology, patching, arithmetic representations or automorphy.
The weight-zero realization bottleneck remains an external/open source obligation, including nonregular limits and the all-local attachment refinement.

mechanisms.summary: Separate the finite automorphic descent fibre once its candidates and distinguishing data have been produced.
boundaries: The source theorem requires an actual automorphic fibre and realizations; a list of symbolic candidate labels is insufficient.
No automorphic Hecke-eigenvalue or descent-fibre constructor exists in the runtime.

mechanisms.summary: A nonnegative integral monomial induction relation would transfer holomorphy from the known entire factors.
boundaries: The runtime stores declared signed terms and detects negative coefficients; it does not solve character-table cone membership or positive saturation.
Holomorphy of the inducing Artin L-functions is external; virtual subtraction does not certify an entire target L-function.

mechanisms.summary: Square-zero ring lift defects are group 2-cocycles; changing lifts adds a coboundary and H2 measures obstruction.
boundaries: Only supplied finite cochain matrices over prime fields or finite linear obstruction systems are executable.

The runtime does not construct the ring-kernel conjugation action, defect cocycle or group-cochain complex automatically; the source square-zero and action hypotheses must be proved for the actual ring.

mechanisms.summary: A distinct H1 obstruction controls gluing local conjugacies after representation lifts exist.
boundaries: A supplied finite cohomology problem can be evaluated; actual local conjugators, global restriction maps and their compatibility are not generated.
Vanishing of an H2 lifting obstruction does not by itself remove this H1 gluing obligation.

mechanisms.summary: Simultaneous polynomial digit correction with nonlinear compatibility and faithful leading-layer hypotheses.
boundaries: Exact prime-field Jacobian fibres and bounded lift towers are integrated; moving syzygy certificates B_x F(x)=0, im J=ker B and faithful principal-ideal layers are not automatic.

The source examples F(x)=(x,x²) and torsion layers distinguish ambient divisibility from internal divisibility; arbitrary compatible target modules are not covered by a free-coordinate prime digit fibre.

mechanisms.summary: The derivative of A↦A^d is the ordered sum ∑ A^j H A^(d−1−j), with a stated ultrametric remainder bound.
boundaries: No dedicated ordered noncommutative power derivative and ultrametric operator-norm remainder certificate API is present.
The bound assumes the specified nonarchimedean norm and unit/radius controls; a complex spectral-norm calculation is a different contract.

mechanisms.summary: A bounded additive inverse Q of the power derivative gives a contraction and unique small-ball root under Kr<1.
boundaries: Current finite numerical correction APIs provide a related finite-dimensional framework, not the source integral two-sided QD=DQ=I matrix-unit certificate or a p-adic ball theorem.
Norm constants, integrality scale, both inverse directions and target membership must be proved; a claimed right inverse alone is insufficient.

mechanisms.summary: Verify one finite compatible filtered branch; record the extra hypotheses needed for a projective-limit endpoint.
boundaries: Finite prime-field branch checks and condition-labelled endpoint records are executable, with exact finite matrix arithmetic.
Compatible joint lifts, compactness, completeness and an infinite branch remain external hypotheses; separate finite forests do not construct a common infinite endpoint.

mechanisms.summary: Source formal mechanisms and verification receipts are distinguished from the conjectural arithmetic realization step.
boundaries: The source formal/research artifacts are not rebuilt or imported as Python kernel proofs by this audit.
Neither the bounded runtime tests nor Boolean gate reports prove Strong Artin or the source unresolved universal realization and all-local attachment statements.

mechanisms.summary: The obstruction P_Hdg−P_Alg and primitive/coniveau reformulations state the rational Hodge target.
boundaries: No runtime constructor computes the actual algebraic-cycle span, rational Hodge subspace or geometric coniveau of an arbitrary smooth projective variety.
A finite matrix projector is useful only after its geometric meaning and rational cycle classes have been established.

mechanisms.summary: For supplied rational cycle-class columns, exact span and positive-frame calculations test coverage of a supplied target subspace.
boundaries: Exact rational matrix rank and full-column-rank frame duals are integrated; actual algebraic cycles, cup-product adjoints and Hodge target bases are external.
Containment of the columns in the target is required for the positive-frame restriction argument. Without containment, use rank[C H]=rank C; canonical_dual rejects deficient rank.

mechanisms.summary: Finite rational analysis/synthesis maps, coefficient projections and exact composition reconstruct supplied packet presentations.
boundaries: This row covers finite rational presentation algebra only; it does not certify that any matrix represents a Chow correspondence or algebraic cycle class.
Degree polyphase, parent/child incidence maps and geometric adjoints still must be supplied with their actual cohomological meaning.

mechanisms.summary: An increasing cycle span in a fixed finite-dimensional ambient space eventually stabilizes at a finite degree.
boundaries: The source existence statement does not give an effective universal stopping degree.
An unchanged observed prefix does not prove that every later algebraic cycle lies in the supplied span.

mechanisms.summary: Support is detected by restriction away from a closed subset and purity supplies lower-dimensional algebraicity transfer.
boundaries: Generic presented-module Fitting support does not implement geometric restriction, purity, cycle support or resolutions of singularities.
An actual variety, closed subset, restriction map and geometric purity hypotheses are required.

mechanisms.summary: Combined lowering maps give T=∑ A†A; invertibility and Cayley–Hamilton furnish a return from lower-degree algebraic data.
boundaries: The finite matrix inversion/composition layer is present; geometric lowering maps, adjoints and actual algebraic correspondences are not constructed.
Positive or invertible finite matrices alone do not supply the required cycle-theoretic maps.

mechanisms.summary: Family propagation, affine pavings, projective bundles, blowups, cubic fourfold and Gushel–Mukai incidence transfers.
boundaries: These rely on specific geometric constructions and classical theorem contracts; no general family, Chow group or incidence-variety implementation is integrated.
Validation examples in the paper are not fresh runtime proofs of general rational Hodge.

mechanisms.summary: Lagrange projectors split supplied Adams eigenvalues m^q into degree packets.
boundaries: Exact primary projectors of supplied finite rational operators are integrated, including nonsemisimple blocks.
Topological K-theory, genuine Adams operations and the geometric cycle identification are external; supplying a matrix with the desired eigenvalues does not construct them.

mechanisms.summary: Range cancellation and the remaining harmonic/Kuranishi obstruction are separated in a finite Lyapunov–Schmidt framework.
boundaries: Current APIs are finite numerical systems. Dolbeault Sobolev spaces, Fredholm gauge splittings, bundle equations and analytic norm estimates are not built.
The source contraction requires 4CM²∥Qf∥<1; range cancellation alone is not a solution unless Π(f+B(a,a))=0.

mechanisms.summary: Unit-orbit balance, rational character packets, gcd conductor deflation and odd prime-power classification.
boundaries: A dedicated Fermat character-tuple balance, unit-orbit census and conductor classifier is absent from the Python runtime.
A balanced tuple proves the expected Hodge type, not the existence of an algebraic cycle representing its rational packet.

mechanisms.summary: Conductor projectors combine power-map graph correspondences through divisor Möbius inversion and gcd product laws.
boundaries: Generic finite spectral projectors are not the actual graph correspondences E_m,d or their normalization 1/(m/d)^5.
Degree inflation can preserve an old conductor; it does not turn a lower-conductor packet into a full-conductor one.

mechanisms.summary: Complementary pairs and balanced four-packets form an exact saturated multiset certificate with an antisymmetric dual obstruction.
boundaries: There is no specialized saturated Fermat multiset solver or dual-charge certificate API.
Even an exact arithmetic grammar identity needs genuine curve/Delsarte/incidence Chow maps; a failed lower grammar is a method obstruction, not nonalgebraicity.

mechanisms.summary: The degree-33 packet (7,10,13,19,22,28) records a failed rejection route and a manuscript Klein–Delsarte constructor.
boundaries: The corrected source branch is included for provenance; it is not integrated as a geometric constructor or independently rebuilt here.
The retracted Newton-data rejection cannot be used to certify a nonalgebraic Hodge class.

mechanisms.summary: Complement triangles, tree/circulation reconstruction, 2-SAT and four-star weighted dyadic certificate families.
boundaries: The source finite research scripts are not an integrated arbitrary weighted-dyadic constructor, and were not freshly replayed in this task.
The current reader explicitly downgrades the earlier uniform writeup; finite dyadic audits do not establish universal reconstructibility.

mechanisms.summary: The bounded global packet census through degree 100 and stated dyadic/weighted finite runs are source evidence.
boundaries: This inventory records the source scope rather than claiming a fresh full replay of its theorem-specific research bundle.
The finite endpoint does not cover arbitrary degree, mixed conductor, or actual cycle constructions beyond each audited family.

mechanisms.summary: Local mod-5 K4/K23 phase grammar, pair–triple sign factorization and imaginary CM selectors identify candidate carriers.
boundaries: No dedicated K4/K23 Fermat phase or CM carrier API is integrated.
Matching a character type or sign pattern does not provide the correctly typed rational Chow correspondence and nonzero target coefficient.

mechanisms.summary: The packet theorem assumes Chow join associativity, Tate-pair removal, resolved Delsarte boundary and nonzero typed constructor coefficients.
boundaries: These geometric assumptions are not certified by generic matrix/grammar computations.
Universal mixed-conductor coverage and the Chow correspondence obligations remain explicit live targets.

mechanisms.summary: A degree-30 weighted carrier with seed (1,20,24,42,61,62) mod 70 carries the stated rational 24-dimensional packet.
boundaries: There is no constructor for the normal weighted hypersurface, cover matrix, mixed-Hodge lift or cycle-class map in the runtime.
Finite monomial, rank or Jacobian checks would still need the source geometric normality, uniruledness and exact correspondence arguments.

mechanisms.summary: An exact multiset transfer from the conductor-70 seed to the conductor-210 target uses pairs, four-packets and standard cycles.
boundaries: The specialized 30-entry signed transfer and its actual Chow correspondences are not implemented; the reported 24/46 source assertions are not this audit’s replay.
Only justified Tate-pair removal is allowed. Arbitrary motivic cancellation and a universal direct matrix constructor are not certified.

mechanisms.summary: A dual weight vector bounds every allowed invariant integer column and proves the specified carrier method capacity obstruction.
boundaries: No specialized infinite-column capacity certificate checker is integrated.
A finite column enumeration is insufficient for the global all-integer-column bound; failure of one matrix method does not prove that the target class is nonalgebraic.

mechanisms.summary: The replacement five-phase family uses actual Aoki complete-intersection surfaces, a uniform Jacobian determinant and a nonzero exact period.
boundaries: The actual surface, containment, complete-intersection, period and rational-orbit reconstruction constructors are absent.
The replacement requires a nonzero cycle coefficient, not just a compatible phase census or finite determinant display.

mechanisms.summary: The explicit Weil sixfold basis/intersection calculations distinguish a failed graph representative from replacement factorizations.
boundaries: There is no general Weil-class geometric or tangent-locus constructor, and the 924-dimensional source replay is not reproduced here.
An obstruction to one graph/representative is not an obstruction to every representative and cannot establish universal nonalgebraicity.

mechanisms.summary: Preserved source Lean scripts certify only their exact formal statement stack when successfully built.
boundaries: The current reader records a build blocked before elaboration by missing compiler/Mathlib; no fresh Lean pass is claimed.
The final abstract algebraicity predicate and seed/closure assumptions do not constitute a general geometric construction or a proof of rational Hodge.

mechanisms.summary: Current source corrections and the live constructor/universality obligations remain visible.
boundaries: No rational Hodge proof or counterexample is claimed by this inventory.
Finite packet identities, exact matrices and source-specific geometric families do not close the general conjecture or universal mixed-conductor constructor target.

mechanisms.summary: Alternating rational partial sums, positive Euler-difference enclosures and integral representations of G.
boundaries: Generic exact sequence sums/differences can be supplied; no specialized Catalan-constant enclosure or integral API is present.
The library’s combinatorial Catalan numbers, Catalan majorants and Apéry ζ(3) recurrence are distinct objects and do not implement these approximants.

mechanisms.summary: A nonzero integer linear form tending to zero contradicts rationality; reduced denominator and exponent margins matter.
boundaries: A finite list of small errors does not establish a nonzero infinite family tending to zero.
Identifying the real limit and classifying its arithmetic nature are different claims.

mechanisms.summary: Execute the exact rational recurrence for u,v with the stated signs and initial pairs.
boundaries: Supply the source-specific ascending coefficient lists; no named Catalan-constant recurrence factory is claimed. The documentation gives the exact adapter.
The library convention is ∑P_j(k)w[k+j]=0; use source n=k+1. Starting the v recurrence at source n=0 would impose an invalid extra initial equation. Executed leading coefficients must be nonzero.

mechanisms.summary: The identification v_n/u_n→G and the characteristic exponential rates are external analytic theorems.
boundaries: An exact finite recurrence prefix does not identify its limit as Catalan’s constant or prove the universal growth/decay rates.
Zudilin source normalization and the distinguished initial pair are part of the contract.

mechanisms.summary: The exact alternating Wronskian controls the adjacent approximant differences and limiting bracket.
boundaries: Finite Wronskians were checked independently in this audit, but there is no dedicated universal bracket/limit theorem API.
Strict rational brackets alone do not imply the limit is irrational. The analytic theorem is still needed to name it G.

mechanisms.summary: The half-binomial sum proves T_n=16^n u_n is integral; the stated v denominator bound is a separate theorem.
boundaries: The recurrence and generic integer/binomial valuation layers are available; no named half-binomial summation/integrality constructor or proof is integrated.
The audit directly checked 25 u rows against an independent generalized-binomial sum and 25 denominator rows. These are finite evidence, not a substitute for the universal integrality proof.

mechanisms.summary: Normalize the published integral by J_n=8(−1)^n(u_nG−v_n), separating the corrected factor from the invalid quarter-factor formula.
boundaries: Whipple/Tonelli and the special-function integral identity are source contracts, not derived by the generic recurrence engine.
The corrected constant and the stated weaker 8·16^n·lcm² clearing versus stronger 4·16^n·lcm² denominator theorem must not be conflated.

mechanisms.summary: Finite Pascal packets S_n,m=∑binom(m,i)T_(n+i), H_n,m and signed integral filters.
boundaries: The exact prefix binomial transform can run a supplied slice; there is no specialized (n,m) Catalan-constant packet API or integral-filter theorem checker.
Even filter order has a source nonzero positive-integral argument; the old universal odd-order sign guess failed. Finite packet arithmetic alone does not prove nonvanishing of forms involving G.

mechanisms.summary: A nonzero residue mod 2^K determines a valuation below K; a zero residue yields only a lower bound.
boundaries: Exact scalar valuations are available; the specialized modular packet scan, precision policy and full-integer controls are not an integrated framework.
A residue of zero does not certify an exact valuation, and a bounded scan cannot prove asymptotic content growth.

mechanisms.summary: Reduce V=N/D and compute h=gcd(DU,N), g=(Q/D)h and the primitive pair (DU/h,N/h).
boundaries: The rational coefficient and packet ingredients are integrated, while the source-specific primitive-content adapter is not a runtime factory.

The audit checked 63 finite packet/content identities with exact Fraction and stdlib gcd/lcm. Extra clearing multiplies content without improving the primitive fraction; content growth must be measured intrinsically.

mechanisms.summary: The even-order asymptotic packet theorem would imply irrationality if the required strict content-growth margin were proved.
boundaries: The sufficient liminf(log g_n)/n inequality is an unproved arithmetic input in this source; analytic decay alone has no adequate cleared margin.
No finite prefix or valuation scan establishes this liminf. This audit does not claim Catalan’s constant irrationality.

mechanisms.summary: Current reader distinguishes corrected normalization, finite research evidence and the remaining asymptotic theorem.
boundaries: This is not recovery of a missing earlier irrationality proof, a fresh replay of all source packet scans, or formal certification.
The exact runtime example validates normalization and finite arithmetic only.

mechanisms.summary: The target is an actual finite Galois field extension L/Q with the full stated automorphism group.
boundaries: A faithful finite representation or a matrix algebra is not a field realization.
The degree |G| alone does not certify separability, normality or the full automorphism group.

mechanisms.summary: The C2,V4,cyclic cubic,S3 and S4 examples require actual polynomial fields and splitting-field/group certification.
boundaries: The library has explicit finite groups but no dedicated rational polynomial number-field or splitting-field certificate constructor.
Discriminants and good-prime factor cycle types require their exact classical hypotheses; toy examples do not establish universal inverse Galois.

mechanisms.summary: Explicit finite groups and regular/coset permutation actions supply finite combinatorial representation data.
boundaries: Finite explicit group operations and induced trivial-character permutation matrices are present; the invariant rational function field and generic Galois field are not.
Numerical representation matrices are not exact field multiplication constants, and the generic fixed field is not automatically Q.

mechanisms.summary: Regular generic fixed fields and rationality/regularity plus Hilbert irreducibility are routes to arithmetic specialization.
boundaries: No invariant-field rationality solver, regular Galois family constructor or Hilbert specialization certificate is integrated.
The Noether rationality problem is not universally true, and a finite sample specialization may collapse the generic group.

mechanisms.summary: Regular representation subgroup averages have fixed rank |G|/|H| and explicit product multiplicity |H∩K|.
boundaries: Finite group and supplied unitary average ingredients exist; no dedicated exact regular subgroup-average/product certificate API is integrated.

quantum.finite_group_projector takes a declared character and unitary matrices and does not infer irreducibility or certify the full representation law. Source subgroup averages require the specified actual regular action.

mechanisms.summary: In the faithful group-algebra realization, average commutation detects HK=KH and centrality detects subgroup normality.
boundaries: Subgroup normality can be checked directly from an explicit finite group; the regular group-algebra equivalence is not automatic for an arbitrary faithful representation.
The source S4 standard representation hides nonnormality through a zero average. Faithful as a group representation is weaker than injective as a group-algebra representation.

mechanisms.summary: Subgroup fixed vectors and averaging projectors do not determine fixed-field multiplication, traces or norms.
boundaries: The runtime has no actual fixed-number-field constructor from these projectors.
Field multiplication constants and the genuine field automorphism action must be retained; vector-space packet dimensions do not supply them.

mechanisms.summary: Finite group extension diagrams distinguish a weak quotient lift from a proper lift whose image contains the full kernel.
boundaries: Explicit finite subgroup images and supplied finite cochain systems can be inspected; a dedicated group-extension/section cocycle factory is absent.
Continuous arithmetic Galois lifts, ramification control and actual proper solutions are external. A weak lift can miss the kernel even when the quotient map is onto.

mechanisms.summary: A realization certificate needs an irreducible rational polynomial, explicit root polynomials, exact field operations and verified distinct group automorphisms.
boundaries: No specialized certificate checker for arbitrary such number fields, normal-basis multiplication tables or polynomial splitting data is integrated.
Matrix action closure, vector-space dimension and a copied group table do not certify irreducibility or produce a field.

mechanisms.summary: Classical solvable realization and specific nonsolvable cases are external theorems; the general finite-group target remains open.
boundaries: The source literature claims and dated M23 state are not independently proof-audited or made current by this local coverage task.
No generic finite-group-to-Q-Galois-field constructor or universal inverse Galois completion is claimed.
